POD DL ROMs are extremely efficient at testing, and that they can be built with a much lower computational cost than conventional ROMs, by relying on multi fidelity pretraining.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
POD DL ROMs can be extremely effective and efficient when dealing with complex nonlinear parametrized problems, by combining the advantages of both POD ROMs and DL ROMs.

, although DL ROMs are able to learn the solution manifold and the reduced order dynamics in a non intrusive manner, POD can be used as an effective tool to further improve their efficiency, especially when dealing with nonlinear parametrized time dependent PDEs.

, when the number of modes of the reduced basis is large enough to ensure an accurate representation of the solution, then the proposed POD DL ROM can be considered a viable alternative to the standard POD ROM, and can provide similar accuracy at a much lower computational cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

POD DL ROMs are a new class of reduced order models which are able to overcome some limitations of classical POD ROMs and which are able to provide a significant computational savings with respect to classical DL ROMs.
we propose a POD DL ROM which combines the best of both worlds, i.e. the accuracy of a deep learning approach and the computational efficiency of a POD approach.
POD DL ROMs are extremely efficient at testing and training time, while preserving the same level of accuracy of standard DL ROMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed POD DL ROMs can be extremely effective when applied to nonlinear parametrized time dependent PDEs, with a computational cost comparable with the one of a standard ROM based on POD, but with a much higher accuracy.
, in many cases, a POD based dimensionality reduction can be performed, and then the resulting reduced system can be efficiently learnt with a deep neural network.

, in order to obtain a DL ROM, one does not need to train a deep neural network from scratch: a POD DL ROM can be trained by combining the information provided by a reduced order model built through POD, and by an additional physical model (which can be a different reduced order model, a full order model, a surrogate model, a numerical solver, or even a physical experiment).
